review.title: Governor may adjourn or prorogue the general court
review.plain: The governor, with advice of council, may adjourn or prorogue the general court as the two houses desire, prorogue it in recess up to ninety days, call it together sooner, and move the session elsewhere in case of infectious distemper or danger. Bracketed wording on dissolving the court in May is printed as superseded.
powers: shall have full power and authority, during the session of the general court to adjourn or prorogue the same
to call it together sooner than the time to which it may be adjourned or prorogued
he may direct the session to be held at some other, the most convenient place within the state
limits: not exceeding ninety days in any one recess

provisions.what: The governor, with advice of council, shall have full power and authority, during the session of the general court to adjourn or prorogue the same to any time the two houses shall desire
provisions.holder: The governor, with advice of council

provisions.what: in the recess of the said court, to prorogue the same from time to time, not exceeding ninety days in any one recess
provisions.holder: The governor, with advice of council
requires: not exceeding ninety days in any one recess
conditions: in the recess of the said court

provisions.what: to call it together sooner than the time to which it may be adjourned or prorogued, if the welfare of the commonwealth shall require the same
provisions.holder: The governor, with advice of council
conditions: if the welfare of the commonwealth shall require the same

provisions.what: he may direct the session to be held at some other, the most convenient place within the state
provisions.holder: The governor
conditions: in case of any infectious distemper prevailing in the place where the said court is next at any time to convene, or any other cause happening whereby danger may arise to the health or lives of the members from their attendance

review.title: Governor settles adjournment disagreements
review.plain: When the two houses disagree about the necessity, expediency or time of adjournment or prorogation, the governor, with the advice of the council, may adjourn or prorogue the general court for up to ninety days, as the public good requires.
powers: shall have a right to adjourn or prorogue the general court

provisions.what: the governor, with the advice of the council, shall have a right to adjourn or prorogue the general court, not exceeding ninety days, as he shall determine the public good shall require
provisions.holder: The governor, with the advice of the council
conditions: In cases of disagreement between the two houses, with regard to the necessity, expediency or time of adjournment, or prorogation

review.title: Governor as commander in chief
review.plain: Annulled: This article made the governor commander in chief of all military forces of the state, with power to train and govern the militia and defend the commonwealth, but barred him from marching inhabitants out of the state without their consent or the general court's. A note says Amendments, Art. LIV annulled and superseded it.

provisions.what: The governor of this commonwealth for the time being, shall be the commander in chief of the army and navy, and of all the military forces of the state, by sea and land, and shall have full power by himself, or by any commander, or other officer or officers, from time to time, to train, instruct, exercise and govern the militia and navy
provisions.holder: The governor
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by See Amendments, Art. LIV.

provisions.what: for the special defence and safety of the commonwealth, to assemble in martial array, and put in warlike posture, the inhabitants thereof, and to lead and conduct them, and with them to encounter, repel, resist, expel and pursue, by force of arms, as well by sea as by land, within or without the limits of this commonwealth
provisions.holder: The governor
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by See Amendments, Art. LIV.

provisions.what: to use and exercise, over the army and navy, and over the militia in actual service, the law martial, in time of war or invasion, and also in time of rebellion, declared by the legislature to exist, as occasion shall necessarily require
provisions.holder: The governor
conditions: in time of war or invasion, and also in time of rebellion, declared by the legislature to exist
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by See Amendments, Art. LIV.

provisions.what: the governor be intrusted with all these and other powers, incident to the offices of captain-general and commander in chief, and admiral, to be exercised agreeably to the rules and regulations of the constitution, and the laws of the land, and not otherwise
provisions.holder: The governor
requires: to be exercised agreeably to the rules and regulations of the constitution, and the laws of the land, and not otherwise
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by See Amendments, Art. LIV.

provisions.what: the said governor shall not, at any time hereafter, by virtue of any power by this constitution granted, or hereafter to be granted to him by the legislature, transport any of the inhabitants of this commonwealth, or oblige them to march out of the limits of the same, without their free and voluntary consent, or the consent of the general court
forbids: transport any of the inhabitants of this commonwealth, or oblige them to march out of the limits of the same, without their free and voluntary consent, or the consent of the general court
exceptions: except so far as may be necessary to march or transport them by land or water, for the defence of such part of the state, to which they cannot otherwise conveniently have access
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by See Amendments, Art. LIV.

review.title: Governor's pardoning power
review.plain: Annulled: This article gave the governor, with the advice of council, the power of pardoning offences, except convictions by the senate on impeachment, and said no pardon granted before conviction would avail the party pleading it. A note says it was annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LXXIII.

provisions.what: The power of pardoning offences, except such as persons may be convicted of before the senate by an impeachment of the house, shall be in the governor, by and with the advice of council
provisions.holder: The governor, by and with the advice of council
exceptions: except such as persons may be convicted of before the senate by an impeachment of the house
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LXXIII.

provisions.what: no charter of pardon, granted by the governor, with advice of the council before conviction, shall avail the party pleading the same, notwithstanding any general or particular expressions contained therein, descriptive of the offence or offences intended to be pardoned
provisions.binds: The governor, with advice of the council
forbids: a charter of pardon granted before conviction availing the party pleading the same
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LXXIII.

review.title: Governor appoints judicial officers
review.plain: All judicial officers, the solicitor-general and coroners shall be nominated and appointed by the governor, with the advice and consent of the council, and each nomination must be made at least seven days before the appointment. Bracketed offices (attorney-general, sheriffs, registers of probate) are printed as superseded.
powers: shall be nominated and appointed by the governor, by and with the advice and consent of the council

provisions.what: All judicial officers, the solicitor-general, coroners, shall be nominated and appointed by the governor, by and with the advice and consent of the council
provisions.holder: The governor, by and with the advice and consent of the council

provisions.what: every such nomination shall be made by the governor, and made at least seven days prior to such appointment
requires: made at least seven days prior to such appointment

review.title: Election and appointment of militia officers
review.plain: Annulled: This article provided for electing militia captains, subalterns, field officers and brigadiers by written votes, appointment of major-generals by the two houses, commissioning by the governor, removal of officers only by address of both houses or court-martial, and other militia appointments and divisions. A note says it was annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

provisions.what: The captains and subalterns of the militia, shall be elected by the written votes of the train band and alarm list of their respective companies, of twenty-one years of age and upwards: the field officers of regiments shall be elected by the written votes of the captains and subalterns of their respective regiments: the brigadiers shall be elected in like manner, by the field officers of their respective brigades: and such officers, so elected, shall be commissioned by the governor, who shall determine their rank
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

provisions.what: The legislature shall, by standing laws, direct the time and manner of convening the electors, and of collecting votes, and of certifying to the governor, the officers elected
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

provisions.what: The major-generals shall be appointed by the senate and house of representatives, each having a negative upon the other; and be commissioned by the governor
provisions.holder: The senate and house of representatives
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

provisions.what: the governor, with advice of council, shall appoint suitable persons to fill such offices
provisions.holder: The governor, with advice of council
conditions: if the electors of brigadiers, field officers, captains or subalterns, shall neglect or refuse to make such elections, after being duly notified, according to the laws for the time being
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

provisions.what: no officer, duly commissioned to command in the militia, shall be removed from his office, but by the address of both houses to the governor, or by fair trial in court-martial pursuant to the laws of the commonwealth for the time being
forbids: removing a duly commissioned militia officer from his office
exceptions: by the address of both houses to the governor, or by fair trial in court-martial pursuant to the laws of the commonwealth for the time being
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

provisions.what: The commanding officers of regiments shall appoint their adjutants and quartermasters; the brigadiers their brigade-majors; and the major-generals their aids; and the governor shall appoint the adjutant-general
provisions.holder: Commanding officers of regiments; brigadiers; major-generals; the governor
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

provisions.what: The governor, with advice of council, shall appoint all officers of the continental army, whom by the confederation of the United States it is provided that this commonwealth shall appoint, as also all officers of forts and garrisons
provisions.holder: The governor, with advice of council
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

provisions.what: The divisions of the militia into brigades, regiments and companies, made in pursuance of the militia laws now in force, shall be considered as the proper divisions of the militia of this commonwealth, until the same shall be altered in pursuance of some future law
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LIII.

review.title: Treasury money only by governor's warrant
review.plain: No money may be issued out of the treasury except by warrant of the governor, with the advice and consent of the council, for the defence and support of the commonwealth and protection of its inhabitants, agreeably to acts of the general court. Sums for redeeming bills of credit or treasurer's notes, or paying their interest, are excepted.
powers: by warrant under the hand of the governor for the time being, with the advice and consent of the council
limits: No moneys shall be issued out of the treasury of this commonwealth, and disposed of

provisions.what: No moneys shall be issued out of the treasury of this commonwealth, and disposed of but by warrant under the hand of the governor for the time being, with the advice and consent of the council, for the necessary defence and support of the commonwealth; and for the protection and preservation of the inhabitants thereof, agreeably to the acts and resolves of the general court
provisions.holder: The governor, with the advice and consent of the council
requires: by warrant under the hand of the governor for the time being, with the advice and consent of the council
agreeably to the acts and resolves of the general court
forbids: issuing moneys out of the treasury of this commonwealth, and disposing of them, but by warrant under the hand of the governor
exceptions: except such sums as may be appropriated for the redemption of bills of credit or treasurer's notes, or for the payment of interest arising thereon

review.title: Reports of public property to the governor
review.plain: Public boards, superintending officers of public magazines and stores, and commanding officers of forts and garrisons must account to the governor every three months, and when required, for all public property in their care, and give him plans of forts. Boards and public officers must pass on public letters and despatches. The bracketed "commissary-general" is printed as superseded.

provisions.what: All public boards, all superintending officers of public magazines and stores, belonging to this commonwealth, and all commanding officers of forts and garrisons within the same, shall once in every three months, officially, and without requisition, and at other times, when required by the governor, deliver to him an account of all goods, stores, provisions, ammunition, cannon with their appendages, and small arms with their accoutrements, and of all other public property whatever under their care respectively
provisions.binds: All public boards, all superintending officers of public magazines and stores, and all commanding officers of forts and garrisons
requires: distinguishing the quantity, number, quality and kind of each, as particularly as may be
together with the condition of such forts and garrisons

provisions.what: the said commanding officer shall exhibit to the governor, when required by him, true and exact plans of such forts, and of the land and sea or harbor or harbors adjacent
provisions.binds: Commanding officers of forts and garrisons

provisions.what: the said boards, and all public officers, shall communicate to the governor, as soon as may be after receiving the same, all letters, despatches, and intelligences of a public nature, which shall be directed to them respectively
provisions.binds: The said boards, and all public officers

review.title: Salaries of the governor and justices
review.plain: So the governor is not dependent on members of the general court, he shall have an honorable stated salary of fixed and permanent value, established by standing laws. Permanent and honorable salaries shall also be established by law for justices of the supreme judicial court, and enlarged if found insufficient.

provisions.what: it is necessary that he should have an honorable stated salary, of a fixed and permanent value, amply sufficient for those purposes, and established by standing laws: and it shall be among the first acts of the general court, after the commencement of this constitution, to establish such salary by law accordingly
Permanent and honorable salaries shall also be established by law for the justices of the supreme judicial court
if it shall be found that any of the salaries aforesaid, so established, are insufficient, they shall, from time to time be enlarged as the general court shall judge proper
conditions: if it shall be found that any of the salaries aforesaid, so established, are insufficient

review.title: Election of the lieutenant governor
review.plain: There shall be an elected lieutenant governor, titled His Honor, qualified in residence like the governor and elected on the same day, in the same manner and by the same electors. If no one is chosen, the senate and house fill the vacancy as for governor. Bracketed words (annually, religion, property, a majority) are printed as superseded.

provisions.what: There shall be elected a lieutenant governor of the commonwealth of Massachusetts, whose title shall be, His Honor and who shall be qualified, in point of residence in the commonwealth, in the same manner with the governor
requires: qualified, in point of residence in the commonwealth, in the same manner with the governor

provisions.what: the day and manner of his election, and the qualifications of the electors, shall be the same as are required in the election of a governor. The return of the votes for this officer, and the declaration of his election, shall be in the same manner
the vacancy shall be filled by the senate and house of representatives, in the same manner as the governor is to be elected
provisions.holder: The senate and house of representatives

review.title: Governor presides over the council
review.plain: The governor, or in his absence the lieutenant governor, is president of the council but has no vote in council. The lieutenant governor is always a member of the council except when the governor's chair is vacant.
limits: shall have no vote in council

provisions.what: The governor, and in his absence the lieutenant governor, shall be president of the council
shall have no vote in council
provisions.binds: The governor, and in his absence the lieutenant governor

provisions.what: the lieutenant governor shall always be a member of the council
exceptions: except when the chair of the governor shall be vacant

review.title: The governor's council
review.plain: There shall be a council to advise the governor in the executive part of government, which the governor may assemble at his discretion. The governor, with at least five councillors, may hold a council to order and direct the commonwealth's affairs according to law. The bracketed number "nine" is printed as superseded.
powers: shall have full power and authority, from time to time, at his discretion, to assemble and call together

provisions.what: There shall be a council for advising the governor in the executive part of government, to consist of persons besides the lieutenant governor
the governor, for the time being, shall have full power and authority, from time to time, at his discretion, to assemble and call together
provisions.holder: The governor

provisions.what: the governor, with the said councillors, or five of them at least, shall and may, from time to time, hold and keep a council, for the ordering and directing the affairs of the commonwealth, according to the laws of the land
provisions.holder: The governor, with the said councillors, or five of them at least
requires: according to the laws of the land

review.title: Choosing councillors
review.plain: Annulled: This article provided that nine councillors be chosen annually by joint ballot of the senators and representatives from those returned as councillors and senators, with any shortfall made up from the people at large, and senators chosen vacating their senate seats. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Art. XVI.

provisions.what: Nine councillors shall be annually chosen from among the persons returned for councillors and senators, on the last Wednesday in May, by the joint ballot of the senators and representatives assembled in one room
changedBy: Superseded by Amendments, Art. XVI.

provisions.what: in case there shall not be found upon the first choice, the whole number of nine persons who will accept a seat in the council, the deficiency shall be made up by the electors aforesaid from among the people at large
changedBy: Superseded by Amendments, Art. XVI.

provisions.what: The seats of the persons thus elected from the senate, and accepting the trust, shall be vacated in the senate
changedBy: Superseded by Amendments, Art. XVI.

review.title: Rank of councillors
review.plain: The councillors, in the civil arrangements of the commonwealth, rank next after the lieutenant governor.

provisions.what: The councillors, in the civil arrangements of the commonwealth, shall have rank next after the lieutenant governor

review.title: Councillors per district
review.plain: Annulled: This article provided that not more than two councillors be chosen out of any one district. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Art XVI.

provisions.what: Not more than two councillors shall be chosen out of any one district of this commonwealth
forbids: choosing more than two councillors out of any one district
changedBy: Superseded by Amendments, Art XVI.

review.title: Council records and dissents
review.plain: The council's resolutions and advice shall be recorded in a register and signed by the members present. Either house of the legislature may call for this record at any time, and any councillor may insert his opinion contrary to the majority's resolution.
rights: any member of the council may insert his opinion, contrary to the resolution of the majority
powers: this record may be called for at any time by either house of the legislature

provisions.what: The resolutions and advice of the council shall be recorded in a register, and signed by the members present
this record may be called for at any time by either house of the legislature
provisions.holder: Either house of the legislature

provisions.what: any member of the council may insert his opinion, contrary to the resolution of the majority
provisions.holder: Any member of the council

review.title: Council acts when both offices are vacant
review.plain: Annulled: This article provided that when the offices of governor and lieutenant governor were both vacant, the council, or most of them, would have full power to do whatever the governor or lieutenant governor could do. A note says it was annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LV.

provisions.what: Whenever the office of the governor and lieutenant governor shall be vacant, by reason of death, absence, or otherwise, then the council, or the major part of them, shall during such vacancy have full power and authority to do, and execute, all and every such acts, matters and things, as the governor or the lieutenant governor might or could, by virtue of this constitution, do or execute
provisions.holder: The council, or the major part of them
conditions: Whenever the office of the governor and lieutenant governor shall be vacant, by reason of death, absence, or otherwise
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LV.

review.title: Order of legislative elections
review.plain: Annulled: This article let the May elections by the two houses be adjourned day to day until completed, and set their order: senate vacancies first, then governor and lieutenant governor if the people made no choice, then the council. A note says it was superseded by Amendments, Arts. XVI and XXV.

provisions.what: the said elections may be adjourned from day to day until the same shall be completed
provisions.holder: The two houses of the legislature
changedBy: Superseded by Amendments, Arts. XVI and XXV.

provisions.what: the order of elections shall be as follows: the vacancies in the senate, if any, shall first be filled up; the governor and lieutenant governor shall then be elected, provided there should be no choice of them by the people: and afterwards the two houses shall proceed to the election of the council
provisions.binds: The two houses of the legislature
changedBy: Superseded by Amendments, Arts. XVI and XXV.

review.title: Choosing secretary, treasurer and other officers
review.plain: Superseded: It provided that the secretary, treasurer and receiver-general, commissary-general, notaries public and naval officers be chosen annually by joint ballot of the senators and representatives, and that no man be eligible as treasurer and receiver-general more than five years successively.

provisions.what: The secretary, treasurer and receiver-general, and the commissary-general, notaries public, and naval officers, shall be chosen annually, by joint ballot of the senators and representatives in one room
provisions.holder: The senators and representatives

provisions.what: no man shall be eligible as treasurer and receiver-general more than five years successively
forbids: being treasurer and receiver-general more than five years successively

review.title: Secretary keeps the records
review.plain: The commonwealth's records shall be kept in the secretary's office. The secretary may appoint deputies, for whose conduct he is accountable, and shall attend the governor and council, the senate and the house, in person or by deputies, as they require.

provisions.what: The records of the commonwealth shall be kept in the office of the secretary
the secretary, who may appoint his deputies, for whose conduct he shall be accountable
provisions.holder: The secretary
requires: for whose conduct he shall be accountable

provisions.what: he shall attend the governor and council, the senate and house of representatives, in person, or by his deputies, as they shall respectively require
